title: Deployment and initialization scripts are treated as protocol code: library-structured, free of hardcoded addresses, and targeting 100% test coverage
content:
A.1.10.2.7.1.1.1 imposes a structure: "Deployment logic must be extracted into a Solidity library that accepts constructor arguments and deploys the contract. Initialization logic must be extracted into a Solidity library that performs post-deployment configuration, including granting roles and setting state. The deployment script must orchestrate the deployment by calling the deployment and initialization libraries" — combined into one library "unless there is reasonable justification for separation."

A.1.10.2.7.1.1.2.1 adds two general requirements: "**Libraries must not contain hardcoded addresses. All addresses and configuration values must be passed as parameters**," and "All library functions must be tested. Test coverage must target 100%."

This elevates deployment from operations to protocol. Deployment scripts usually live outside the reviewed artifact — written quickly, run once, discarded — yet they determine constructor arguments, role grants and initial state, which is to say most of what a module actually does in practice. A perfectly audited contract deployed with the wrong role grant is a compromised contract.

Banning hardcoded addresses is the sharpest of these rules. It separates *logic* from *configuration*, so the audited artifact is a reusable mechanism and every address becomes a visible input reviewable at the call site rather than a constant buried in code where a single wrong character reads as normal.

A.1.10.2.7.1.1.2.2 completes it by requiring deployment scripts to "yield ownership of deployed contracts to the relevant Governance proxy" and putting top-level deployment scripts in audit scope, with auditors verifying constructor parameters at minimum.
description: A.1.10.2.7.1.1 forces deployment logic out of ad hoc scripting into auditable Solidity libraries where every address is a parameter, so configuration is reviewable rather than embedded.
